haiku-low.q1: Sign-in still works. Matching is by Google sub only, so the changed Gmail address changes nothing and the linked account signs in.
haiku-low.q2: The user must enter the existing account's password on the confirm page. Only a correct password inserts the link, and then the session starts.
haiku-low.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins. At the fifth, locked_until is set to now plus 15 minutes and the pending link and glink cookie are deleted.
haiku-low.q4: A verified email matching no user creates a new user with NULL password_hash and a linked identity, then signs in. Unverified email: login page says use email and password, nothing created.
haiku-low.q5: At 12 minutes the attempt has expired, so an error page shows and nothing changes. A second load finds nothing, since GETDEL consumed the attempt, so it also shows an error page.
haiku-low.q6: A new sessions row and sid cookie, the same as password login. Any sid row named by the browser's existing sid cookie is deleted, so the old session is replaced.
haiku-low.q7: Neither is required, since the user is already signed in. If that Google sub is linked to another user, the link is refused and nothing changes.
haiku-low.q8: state, nonce and PKCE verifier are in Redis under goog:attempt:{state} with TTL 600 s. The gstate cookie holds state. GETDEL at the callback or TTL expiry removes them.
haiku-low.q9: In Redis at goog:pending:{pid} holding sub, user_id and next. The browser refers to it by the glink cookie holding pid. Success, lockout, refusal or TTL expiry deletes it.
haiku-low.q10: In PostgreSQL table google_identities. sub as primary key limits one Google account to one user; UNIQUE(user_id) limits one user to one Google account.
haiku-low.q11: The user sees a neutral try-again message on the origin page and the failure is logged. Nothing is created or linked. The exchange is not retried, since the code is single use.
haiku-low.q12: The stored attempt's mode (login or link) decides the branch. In link mode the callback checks the signed-in user is the attempt's user_id; otherwise it shows an error page and changes nothing.

sonnet.q1: Nothing changes. Matching is by `sub` only, so the linked google_identities row is found and the user is signed in via start_session; a changed Google email changes nothing (users.email is untouched).
sonnet.q2: If the user has no Google account linked: the callback makes a pending link (goog:pending:pid in Redis, glink cookie) and redirects to the confirm page, where the user must enter the account's password. Only a correct password (when not locked) inserts the google_identities row, deletes pending and glink, and calls start_session. If that user already has a Google linked, it is refused.
sonnet.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins, the confirm form shows again with the same pending link (TTL not extended). On the fifth, locked_until is set to now + 15 minutes, failed_logins resets to 0, and the pending key and glink cookie are deleted with a locked message. If the account is already locked, the pending link is deleted and the password is not checked. No link is made.
sonnet.q4: Verified email matching no user: one transaction inserts a new user with NULL password_hash and email_verified_at now, plus a google_identities row, then start_session (a unique conflict gives a try-again message). If email_verified is false or missing: nothing is created, and the login page tells the user to use email and password.
sonnet.q5: Error page and nothing changes. A state that is expired (over 10 minutes, TTL), reused or missing finds nothing in Redis because GETDEL consumed it or it expired.
sonnet.q6: The same kind of session as a password login, since it goes through start_session: a new sessions row and a sid cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax). Any sessions row named by an incoming sid cookie is deleted first, so a user already signed in as someone else is replaced. Then redirect to next if relative, else /home.
sonnet.q7: No password and no email match is needed (the user is already signed in; no verified email is needed). If the sub is linked to another user, it is refused (Settings message, nothing changes). If it is already linked to this user, the message is 'already linked'. No session is created.
sonnet.q8: In Redis under goog:attempt:{state} holding {code_verifier, nonce, mode, user_id (link mode only), next}, TTL 600 s. The browser also holds the gstate cookie (= state, Max-Age 600). The attempt is removed by GETDEL at the callback or by TTL; gstate is cleared at the callback or expires.
sonnet.q9: In Redis at goog:pending:{pid} = {sub, user_id, next}, TTL 600 s (not extended by wrong passwords). The browser refers to it with the glink cookie holding pid; confirm finds it by that cookie only. It is deleted on success, lockout (new or already active), refusal (unique conflict), or TTL; glink is cleared whenever the key is deleted, or it expires.
sonnet.q10: In the PostgreSQL table google_identities(sub PK, user_id NOT NULL UNIQUE -> users ON DELETE CASCADE, created_at). sub as primary key means one Google account links to at most one user, and UNIQUE(user_id) means one user has at most one Google account.
sonnet.q11: The user is sent back to the origin (login page or Settings) with a neutral try-again message. The exchange is not retried, because the code is single use, so the user starts a new attempt. The failure is logged and nothing is created or linked; the attempt is already consumed.
sonnet.q12: The mode (login or link) is stored in the Redis attempt and read at the callback. For link mode the attempt stores user_id of the signed-in user who started; the callback requires the currently signed-in user to equal that user_id, otherwise it shows the error page. The link row is inserted for that user_id.
